Qualified Retired Persons program (QRP) documentation shape
value_raw: Program application fee US$150, applicant fee US$1,000 (US$750/dependent), the program's own ID card (QRP card) US$200/card, annual renewal US$25; a Ministry of National Security security-clearance check; and — per the program's own qualifying-income list (Pension, Annuity, Social Security Benefits, Investment Account, Inheritance, Reverse Mortgage, Personal Savings, Retirement Contribution Plans, and other means of retirement income) — proof the qualifying $2,000/month is drawn from one of these named sources. A real, documented practical hurdle beyond the paper checklist: at least one applicant account describes the $2,000/month needing to be shown as 'forwarded to a reputable financial institution within Belize,' which creates a catch-22 for applicants who can't open a Belizean bank account until residency status is further along — resolved in that one case only by appealing directly to the Central Bank via a correspondent bank.

No fixed document checklist tied to a dollar threshold — Belize's Department of Immigration requires an arrival stamp at least one (1) year old at time of application, plus proof, to the Immigration Officer's discretion, of financial stability (no cumulative-absence-days cap could be confirmed on the primary source), demonstrated across what the official permanent-residency (PR) requirements page describes as eight recognized categories (only two named in the held record: 'employment by a Belize business,' and sponsorship by a qualified individual, e.g. a legally married Belizean/PR-holding spouse whose income-tax letter serves as supporting proof) — the other six categories are not enumerated in the held source. Also requires no criminal conviction carrying a potential 12+ months' imprisonment, in any country.
